rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At resurrection, criminals expect false oaths to prove their innocence as they did in the world, but sealed tongues and witnessing limbs expose them and leave no excuse.
rows.anchor: by swearing false oaths they will think that they have furnished a very strong argument in favour of their innocence

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an identifies them as actual liars who deceived people in this life and will audaciously try to deceive God in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: They are the real liars, and have deceived others in this world because of their lies

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan suggests evil to everyone, but only those who welcome him as guide and counsellor are led astray and become his faction.
rows.anchor: only those who open their hearts to them, and regard Satan to be their guide and counsel are led away by these suggestions

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s disciples become empty of remembrance of God; remembering God is a person's real protection, and losing it leaves one trapped by Satan.
rows.anchor: The real protection of a person is God’s remembrance. After being deprived of it, he is lured away by Satan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although Satan’s faction receives time to spread mischief under God’s law of respite, it is ultimately doomed.
rows.anchor: ultimately the faction of Satan is destined to doom

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who oppose God and His Prophet grow more antagonistic during their respite, but end among the humiliated.
rows.anchor: they will end up among those who had been humiliated earlier on by showing this attitude

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every rasūl, unlike a nabī, embodies divine justice and settles his people's fate: rejection brings destruction after migration, or, with many believers, post-proof warfare; Muḥammad's was the latter case, while most messengers faced the former.
rows.anchor: every messenger (rasūl) (as opposed to nabī (prophet)) sent by God to his people is a symbol of divine justice

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s power explains why He and His messengers must prevail: obedience to the real king’s envoy brings earthly sovereignty and favour, while opposition after proof makes a people rebels whom God removes.
rows.anchor: God is not a weak being: He is Powerful and Mighty.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sets a test for hypocrites: belief in God and the Hereafter cannot coexist with friendship toward their opponents, since one heart cannot hold opposing loyalties.
rows.anchor: A person only has one heart not two and he cannot harbour two opposing and contradictory things in one heart.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even natural affection for a father, son, brother, or other close relative cannot justify giving an opponent of one's faith a place in one's heart.
rows.anchor: even the father, the son, the brother and other close of relatives of the family

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who apply this test to themselves have faith etched in their hearts and receive God's special spiritual help.
rows.anchor: people who are ready to evaluate themselves or who let others evaluate them as per this standard

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who claim faith while maintaining ties with God's and His Messenger's enemies are Muslims in name only, with hearts unfamiliar with faith.
rows.anchor: they are Muslims in name only; their hearts are not conversant with the faith

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because family and tribal attachments run deep, God gives believers special spiritual aid in this difficult trial so they can pass it.
rows.anchor: It is not easy at all to sever it. However, when people whose hearts are alive with the sanctity

rows.speaker: Ḥāfiẓ Shirāẓi
rows.claim: As corroboration for divine spiritual aid, the author quotes Ḥāfiẓ Shirāẓi: with the Holy Spirit's blessing, one can do what Jesus did.
rows.anchor: and they come out of this test with flying colours. To quote Ḥāfiẓ Shirāẓi:27

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Examples of allegiance to faith over kinship include Abū ʿUbaydah confronting his father at Uḥud, Abū Bakr challenging his son at Badr, Muṣʿab and ʿUmar killing close relatives, and ʿAlī, Ḥamzah, and Abū ʿUbaydah killing Quraysh kin.
rows.anchor: raised his sword against his father

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of eternal Paradise means God grants these people strong faith and spiritual gains, enabling them to persevere on truth until death.
rows.anchor: these people were blessed by God with strong faith and spiritual gains and made them persevere in the path of truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pleasure is their greatest reward because they fulfilled their professed obligations, passed every trial, and displayed the character He required.
rows.anchor: The Almighty will be pleased with them because they duly fulfilled the obligations of the faith they laid claim to and passed in each trial

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their being pleased with God means the promises they lived and died upon will be fulfilled far beyond expectation, satisfying all their desires.
rows.anchor: The fact that they were pleased with God means that the promises on which they lived and died

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only these people deserve to be called God's faction and will succeed; after describing Satan's faction, the sūra ends with God's faction.
rows.anchor: it is these people who will be worthy of being counted among the faction of God, and it is they only who will succeed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author closes by praying that God reveal truth and falsehood clearly, enable adherence to truth, and help avoid falsehood.
rows.anchor: Show us the truth the way it is and make us follow it and show us falsehood the way it is

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥashr demonstrates the previous sūra's claim that opponents of God and His Messenger are humbled while God and His messengers prevail, using Banū Naḍīr's panic, self-demolition, exile, and abandonment as a warning to hypocrites.
rows.anchor: the previous sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra ends by saying the Qur’an was revealed to dispel doubts and soften hearts; a mountain would crumble from fear of God, so hearts unmoved by it are harder than stone and merit God's treatment of the stone-hearted.
rows.anchor: on a mountain, it would have been crushed to pieces because of the fear of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banū Naḍīr were exiled for breaking their covenant and plotting to kill the Prophet; after initially accepting punishment, they changed their minds when allies offered help, and the Prophet attacked in year four of the Hijra, sending them to Khaybar with what their camels could carry.
rows.anchor: they had broken their covenant and had plotted to kill the Prophet (sws)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Banū Naḍīr's fate warns hypocrites who thought the Jews could not be expelled: the Prophet's opponents meet this end, and those who seek Jewish support will share it.
rows.anchor: By citing their example, the hypocrites have been admonished to seek a lesson from this event

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verses 5–10 form a parenthetical digression answering objections about the Banū Naḍīr incident raised by Jews and hypocrites.
rows.anchor: In a parenthetical sentence, certain objections raised by the Jews and

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incident should teach that God's and His Prophet's enemies were humiliated and God's faction prevailed; those still wishing to befriend them should consider the consequences.
rows.anchor: how clearly God’s faction prevailed over Satan’s faction

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exile was lenient punishment, deliberately leaving Banū Naḍīr an opportunity to learn; otherwise God could have destroyed them as He did ʿĀd, Thamūd, and Pharaoh, and their failure to reform brings compensating Hellfire.
rows.anchor: was in fact a show of lenience to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The suppressed words “and His Messenger” after “whoever opposes God” show that enmity toward the Prophet is tantamount to enmity toward God.
rows.anchor: showing enmity to the Prophet (sws) is tantamount to showing enmity to God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion of verses 5–10 is a parenthetical digression from the main topic, addressing Jewish and hypocrite objections to the Banū Naḍīr episode.
rows.anchor: In this section, which forms a parenthetical sentence and is a digression from the main topic

rows.speaker: the Jews
rows.claim: The Jews objected that Muslims had chopped down fruit-bearing trees, portraying their wartime felling as anarchy in the land.
rows.anchor: The Jews tried to portray the incident as spreading anarchy in the land
